transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-28
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood CSM), Sofia Martinez (Globex VP Eng), Daniel Kim (Globex SRE), Rachel Lee (Globex Platform), Evan Torres (Globex Security)
Links shared: incident-report-v1.docx (link), runbook-draft.md (link), bench-specs.xlsx (link)

[00:00] Maya Chen: okay thanks everyone for taking the time. we wanted to walk through the postmortem followup, clarify mitigations, and agree next steps. Sofia, do you want to kick off with how things looked from Globex side?

[00:18] Sofia Martinez: yeah thanks Maya. overall the outage on 3/20 impacted our prod API for about 2 hours with elevated p95 latency and some 5xx errors. we lost partial traf to our recommendation engine. Daniel can share specifics but top line—users saw timeouts at peak.

[00:33] Daniel Kim: yeah so from our observability the outage started around 10:12 UTC and you can see a spike in token latency and repeated retries. our KV cache hit rate dropped from 92% to about 11% after what we think was a cache invalidation cascade then the autoscaler started spinning up nodes which then hit OOMs on several pods.

[00:55] Arjun Patel: thanks, that's consistent with the traces we pulled. there was a race in the cache invalidation handler plus an aggressive autoscaler threshold that caused multiple scale-up events and inconsistent model shard placement. the runtime then dropped into a high memory tail leading to OOMs for some requests.

[01:20] Rachel Lee: to add, our config had the default cache ttl set lower for some routes, and when traffic shifted the prefix caching didn't warm quickly which amplified requests to cold KV.

[01:38] Maya Chen: okay got it. so root causes we're triangulating are: a cache invalidation edge-case, autoscaler sensitivity + placement bug, and some config defaults that made warmup slower. is that fair?

[01:52] Sofia Martinez: yes that's fair. the customer impact was material—we escalated to execs because the recommender is core to our paid conversion flows.

[02:06] Liam O'Connor: on Redwood side we want to own the mitigation path. we've already shipped a hotfix to reduce the aggressive threshold and add a backoff to the scale-up path. Arjun, can you summarize the patch?

[02:20] Arjun Patel: sure—patch v1.2.7 changes the autoscaler policy to include a 30s cooldown between scale-up attempts, adds a placement verification step before marking a node healthy, and fixes the cache invalidation handler so it does batched invalidations instead of per-key ops which was the major amplification vector. we've validated in our internal staging with a synthetic spike and saw cache hit rate recover to above 85% within 90s and no OOMs.

[02:58] Daniel Kim: happy to hear staging looked good. did you also change the KV client retry/backoff semantics? we saw retries causing extra load.

[03:08] Arjun Patel: yes we reduced immediate retry bursts by switching to jittered exponential backoff and added a token-bucket limiter for cache fill operations from the runtime, that prevents a stampede.

[03:25] Sofia Martinez: excellent. question—what's the plan for pushing the hotfix to our dedicated cluster? we can't do sudden restarts during prime windows.

[03:34] Maya Chen: agreed, so proposed plan: 1) push hotfix to staging in your VPC next week, run the bench with your traffic profile; 2) then canary to a subset of pods (10%) off-peak; 3) full rollout with continuous monitoring and rollback window. we'll coordinate windows with Liam.

[03:56] Rachel Lee: for the bench run we need to confirm the infra specs—will you use Redwood dedicated cluster or bring-your-own? we want this to mirror our production as much as possible.

[04:10] Liam O'Connor: goal is to run on a dedicated cluster provisioned with same GPU class and model shard counts. I'll own scheduling and VM sizes. we have bench-specs.xlsx we can fill with the exact numbers—Arjun please confirm you can run the same images.

[04:28] Arjun Patel: yes same docker images and runtime flags; we'll share the exact build id for the hotfix and the bench harness commands.

[04:38] [05:00] Sofia Martinez: two security questions—KMS integration and audit logs. Evan?

[05:04] Evan Torres: yeah. we need to ensure keys are customer-managed, and that access is logged to our SIEM. also want to validate RBAC for model deployments—only our ops should be able to trigger rollouts.

[05:20] Maya Chen: we support customer KMS and HSM integrations; Redwood will send KMS integration docs. for audit logs we can push to your S3 or SIEM via secure forwarder and provide search access in console exports. RBAC is supported via SSO + SAML and fine-grained roles—Arjun will share config examples.

[05:40] Daniel Kim: would also appreciate a runbook with steps to toggle to fallback model variants or reduce concurrency in emergencies.

[05:48] Arjun Patel: we've got a runbook-draft.md link in the chat. it includes steps to switch routing policies to the cheaper low-latency variant, cache flush avoidance patterns, and how to toggle autoscaler thresholds. note it's a draft—we'll iterate with your SRE.

[06:10] Sofia Martinez: perfect, please make sure the runbook has explicit CLI snippets—our oncall needs commands they can paste.

[06:22] [09:00] Rachel Lee: small nit—during the incident we lost some trace metadata because the KV invalidation raced with tracing flush; can we ensure traces survive cache clears? it's hard to debug without them.

[06:35] Arjun Patel: good catch. we'll add trace forwarders that keep trace IDs on cache invalidation operations and store them in a short-lived buffer for 15 minutes so you still get context. we'll also add instrumentation to alert when trace-drop rates exceed threshold.

[06:55] Maya Chen: circling back to commercial impact—Sofia you mentioned exec escalations; can you quantify financial or SLA hits so we can include credits in proposal?

[07:07] Sofia Martinez: early estimate: about 4% conversion loss over the two hour window; roughly $18k revenue impact for the week, plus internal ops costs. we'll validate and share numbers with Maya.

[07:20] Liam O'Connor: we'll take that into account and draft a one-time credits proposal and ETA for a follow-up health credit if we see repeat windows.

[07:33] [15:00] Daniel Kim: on long-term reliability, are there recommended config changes to prevent warmup slowness? you'd mentioned cache ttl defaults—should we bump to X?

[07:44] Arjun Patel: recommendation: increase prefix cache pre-warm to 60s for high-volume routes, tune the cache TTL to avoid aggressive evictions, and enable proactive KD (key distribution) warming during deployment. also consider enabling local LRU caching for very hot prefixes. we'll provide a recommended config file.

[08:05] Sofia Martinez: can Redwood automate prefix warming during deployment? that would reduce warmup pain especially during rollouts.

[08:13] Arjun Patel: yes we have a feature flag for automated warmups that triggers synthetic requests for pinned prefixes; we'll enable it for your canary and show results.

[08:24] [22:30] Rachel Lee: about monitoring—we need token-level cost telemetry and per-route latency percentiles exposed. does the console give that?

[08:36] Maya Chen: yes Console has token-level cost, per-route/model dashboards, and tracing hooks. we can add a custom panel for Globex with alerts on p95 and cache hit rate. Liam will set up access.

[08:49] Evan Torres: one more security ask: will the patched autoscaler changes require additional cert rotation or will it touch network config?

[08:58] Arjun Patel: no network changes. the patch is runtime-level and autoscaler config; it does not rotate certs. KMS integration is separate and won't be impacted.

[09:10] Maya Chen: good. let's walk through agreed timeline: Arjun will validate patch in staging by Apr 2; Daniel will provide traffic profile by Mar 31; bench run scheduled week of Apr 7; SOC2/KMS docs sent by Apr 1; commercial credits proposal by Apr 3. anything missing?

[09:32] Sofia Martinez: please include a 60-minute post-bench sync to go over metrics after bench.

[09:40] Maya Chen: noted. we'll add that.

[09:46] [44:00] Summary / Recap (auto):
- Root causes: cache invalidation cascade, autoscaler scale-up sensitivity + placement bug, config defaults exacerbating warmup.
- Immediate mitigations: autoscaler cooldown & placement verification, batched invalidations, jittered retries, token-bucket limiter.
- Validation: internal staging passed synthetic spike; bench run planned on dedicated cluster.
- Security: KMS/HSM supported, RBAC via SSO, audit logs export supported.
- Next steps and action items captured above; links to runbook and incident report were shared in chat.

[44:30] Next steps (spoken):
Maya Chen: we'll send the incident timeline and final runbook by EOD tomorrow, and Arjun will push the staging build id. Liam will coordinate bench dates. thanks everyone.

[44:50] Sofia Martinez: thanks, appreciate swift response. will share conversion numbers and traffic profile.

[45:00] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: some proper nouns may be slightly off; timestamps are approximate.
